files.purpose: CopilotSession is the @MainActor ProviderSession that drives the GitHub Copilot CLI as a child process started with `--headless --stdio`, speaking the Copilot SDK's Content-Length framed JSON-RPC protocol (one process per thread, session created or resumed under Droppy Code's own lowercased UUID so history survives relaunches in `~/.copilot/session-state`). It maps the CLI's `session.event` notifications (assistant deltas, reasoning, usage, tool execution, sub-agents, permissions, mode/title changes, errors, compaction, idle, shutdown) onto ProviderEvent values, answers the CLI's server requests (`userInput.request`, `exitPlanMode.request`, `autoModeSwitch.request`), translates Droppy's RuntimeMode/InteractionMode, model and effort into CLI RPCs, and implements approvals, questions, interrupt, compaction, rewind-based rollback and slash-command invocation. It also exposes static one-shot helpers that spawn a throwaway connection in the temp directory to list models (`models.list`), read sign-in status (`account.getCurrentAuth`) and read plan limits (`account.getQuota`), plus pure mapping helpers (tool-call titles, apply_patch path extraction, update_todo checklist parsing, permission descriptions, session-approval decisions, error-message enrichment). With Hydra on it creates the session with custom agents, appends the Hydra policy to the system message and forwards head (sub-agent) events wrapped in `.agentEvent`.

Then session.history.listRewindPoints, picks points[points.count - turns].eventId (needs points.count >= turns), else throws "Copilot has no rewind point for that turn."; then session.history.rewind {sessionId, eventId, mode: "conversation"}; outcome != "success" throws result.error ?? "Copilot could not rewind the conversation.". Files are not touched (Droppy checkpoints restore them).

connect(): JSONRPCConnection(sendsVersion: true); ping {message: "droppy-code"}; missing protocolVersion closes and throws "This `copilot` does not speak the SDK protocol. Update it with `copilot update`."

handleNotification (lines 504-518): only method "session.event"; reads params.sessionId, params.event.type, params.event.agentId and params.event.data (data defaults to .null); ignores events whose sessionId differs from ours. Sub-agent events (agentId set) of type assistant.* or tool.* except assistant.usage are dropped when configuration.hydra == nil. `sink` wraps in .agentEvent(agentID:) when agentId is set, else is leadSink (= onEvent). Only assistant.turn_start (agent branch), assistant.message_delta, assistant.message, assistant.reasoning_delta, assistant.reasoning and tool.* go through sink. assistant.usage, session.usage_info, subagent.*, permission.* and session.* call onEvent directly, so a head's spend is a top-level .tokenSpend carrying agentID, not an .agentEvent.

assistant.usage: spend = inputTokens + outputTokens; TokenSpend(provider: .copilot, totalTokens, inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedInputTokens: cacheReadTokens, model: data.model ?? model, agentID). session.usage_info -> ContextUsage(usedTokens: currentTokens, windowTokens: tokenLimit).

session.mode_changed newMode "plan" -> .plan; "interactive"/"autopilot" -> .build. session.error stored as turnError while a turn is active, else an error notice. session.idle -> finishTurn(aborted:). session.shutdown with shutdownType "error" posts errorReason as an error notice.

handleMessage: reasoningText shown as "<id>-reasoning" only if non-whitespace and not already shown (trimmed hash); messageCompleted when content non-empty or deltas streamed; toolRequests replayed through toolRequested.

toolRequested: de-duplicated by call id; update_todo emits .todos parsed from arguments.todos and no row; task stores brief (description ?? name ?? "Subagent", prompt ?? task); emits toolStarted and a toolUpdated with edits when present.
handleToolResult: hidden tools ignored; success defaults true; output = error.message on failure else result.detailedContent ?? result.content; status completed / declined / failed.

finishTurn(aborted:) (lines 695-715): `guard turnActive else { return }`, so a session.idle outside a turn emits nothing. Sets turnActive = false, clears toolNames, declinedTools, taskBriefs and shownReasoning (not streamedMessages), cancels pending requests; turnCompleted status .interrupted if aborted or interruptRequested, .failed with turnError, else .completed; resets interruptRequested.

errorMessage: default "Copilot reported an error."; after "GenericFailure, " parses JSON {status, body} into "HTTP <status>: <trimmed body>"; statusCode 403, remediation "sign_in" or "not authorized to use this Copilot feature" appends " Check that your GitHub account has Copilot access, or sign in again with `copilot login`."
handleRequest: autoModeSwitch.request answered {response: "no"}; unknown methods get error -32601 "Droppy Code does not support <method>."; plan content = planContent (non-empty) ?? summary ?? "".

handlePermission: ignores resolvedByHook; automaticDecision first ({kind: "approve-once"}: fullAccess always; autoAcceptEdits for kind write/read; auto for write/read or assistedApproval.recommendation == "approve" from promptRequest or request; supervised never); a write prompt with a diff updates the tool row with the CLI's patch and diffStats; reason falls back to promptRequest.assistedApproval.reason.

sessionApproval: shell needs canOfferSessionApproval and commands[].identifier -> {kind: "commands", commandIdentifiers}; write needs canOfferSessionApproval -> {kind: "write"}; read -> {kind: "read"}; url -> returns {kind: "approve-for-session", domain: host} directly; mcp -> {kind: "mcp", serverName, toolName}; custom-tool -> {kind: "custom-tool", toolName}; memory -> {kind: "memory"}; wrapped as {kind: "approve-for-session", approval}.

cancelPendingRequests: permission -> {kind: "cancelled", reason: "The user stopped the turn."}; question -> error -32800 "The user stopped the turn."; plan -> {approved: false, feedback: "The user stopped the turn."}.

handleClose (lines 931-938): emits .requestResolved for every pending key WITHOUT answering it (the connection is gone), clears pendingRequests and turnActive, emits no .turnCompleted, and unless isStopping emits .exited(error: TextCleanup.lastLines(tail)).

toolCall mapping covers MCP ("<server> · <tool>"), bash/powershell, read_bash/write_bash/stop_bash/list_bash, view, create, edit, str_replace_editor (view/create/insert/default), apply_patch, grep, glob, web_fetch, web_search, task, read_agent/write_agent/list_agents, skill, sql, create_pull_request, and a default humanized row with single-line compact arguments.

patchPaths: headers "*** Update File: ", "*** Add File: ", "*** Delete File: ", de-duplicated in order. todos: pattern accepts -, *, + or N. / N) bullets; [x]/[X] done, [ ] or [] pending, anything else active.
humanize: '-' and '_' to spaces, first character uppercased.

B1->B2: Five mechanical changes, no behavior change except date parsing. (1) invokeCommand line 218 uses `text.trimmed.isEmpty` instead of trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines); (2) slashCommand lines 233 and 235 use `.trimmed`; (3) parseDate (lines 470-472) now returns `ISO8601.date(from: text) ?? ISO8601.dateOnly(from: text)` instead of building an ISO8601DateFormatter and retrying with formatOptions [.withFullDate]; the shared ISO8601.date accepts both fractional and whole-second stamps (the old default ISO8601DateFormatter did not accept fractional seconds); file shrank from 1075 to 1072 lines; (4) errorMessage line 724 uses `body.trimmed`; (5) reasoningKey line 1065 uses `text.trimmed.hashValue`. `.trimmed` is defined in Core/Support/Text.swift as trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines), so those four are equivalent.

isExperimentalMode is a session setting (comment lines 117-120): "the thread restarts the session when it switches into or out of Auto". The restart is done by the caller; applyModes alone does not toggle experimental mode.

assistant.turn_start (lines 520-526): with an agentId -> sink(.turnStarted(providerTurnID: data["turnId"])); without one and when !turnActive -> turnActive = true and onEvent(.turnStarted(providerTurnID: data["turnId"])), i.e. a turn the CLI began itself. That path skips beginTurn(), so turnError, interruptRequested, streamedMessages and shownReasoning are not reset.

Wire keys per event: assistant.message_delta data.messageId + data.deltaContent (id inserted in streamedMessages, .messageDelta); assistant.reasoning_delta data.reasoningId + data.deltaContent (.reasoningDelta); assistant.reasoning data.reasoningId + data.content (default "", key inserted in shownReasoning, .reasoningCompleted); assistant.usage data.inputTokens/outputTokens/cacheReadTokens/model; session.usage_info data.currentTokens/tokenLimit; tool.execution_start data.toolCallId/toolName/arguments/mcpServerName/mcpToolName; tool.execution_complete data.toolCallId/success/error.message/result.detailedContent/result.content; subagent.* data.toolCallId/agentDisplayName/agentName/model, subagent.completed data.cancelled, subagent.failed data.error (summary); session.idle data.aborted; session.mode_changed data.newMode; session.title_changed data.title (non-empty); session.shutdown data.shutdownType/errorReason; permission.requested data.requestId/permissionRequest/promptRequest/resolvedByHook, permissionRequest.toolCallId/kind/diff/resolvedPath/fileName; handleMessage data.messageId/reasoningText/content/toolRequests[].{toolCallId,name,arguments,mcpServerName,mcpToolName}.

tool.execution_partial_result (lines 569-572): data.toolCallId + data.partialOutput -> sink(.toolOutput(id:text:)). tool.execution_progress (lines 573-576): data.toolCallId + data.progressMessage -> sink(.toolUpdated(id:, update: ToolUpdate(detail: message))).

permission.completed (lines 599-602): `if let requestID = data["requestId"]?.string, pendingRequests.removeValue(forKey: requestID) != nil { onEvent?(.requestResolved(id: requestID)) }`, so an approval the CLI resolved itself leaves the UI.

session.warning (lines 623-624): data.message -> Notice(level: .warning). session.compaction_complete (lines 625-630): success == true -> info "Context compacted."; otherwise data.error (when present) -> warning notice with that text.
exitPlanMode.request (lines 753-767): stores .planExit under "plan-<id.key>", emits .planCompleted(id: key, markdown: plan) BEFORE the .approval (kind .plan).
unresolved_questions: Exact shape of MCPSessionOverrides.copilotArguments() and HydraPrompts.copilotAgents output is defined elsewhere and not verified here.
How the Windows port will locate and launch the `copilot` CLI (npm shim .cmd vs node entry) with Content-Length stdio framing is outside this file.

files.purpose: DeepSeekAPI is a caseless enum holding the lightweight HTTP calls for the DeepSeek OpenAI-compatible API that the provider registry needs outside a chat session: key validation, model catalog listing, and the prepaid balance read for the usage panel. It also owns the static DeepSeek model catalog policy: which ids map to named ModelOptions, which retired ids are hidden, the shared effort list, the 1M context window, and which ids accept images (chat streaming itself lives in DeepSeekSession).

files.purpose: MetaAPI is a caseless enum with the lightweight HTTP calls for Meta's OpenAI-compatible Muse API at https://api.meta.ai/v1 (key validation and model listing) used by the provider registry, while chat streaming lives in MetaSession. It also fixes the Muse Spark catalog policy: context and output token limits, per-model effort lists (only muse-spark-1.3 gets "max"), named options for known checkpoints, a filter that drops non-chat Muse models, and the vision check.

files.purpose: NativeFileTools is a Sendable struct bound to a project working directory that implements the file tools Droppy's native API providers expose to models: read_file, write_file, edit_file and list_files, plus the path resolution that confines every model-supplied path to the project root. Reads are capped at 1,000,000 bytes and long text is truncated to 60,000 characters with a line-range hint; writes and edits are serialised through a private static actor so concurrent tool calls cannot interleave mutations, and edits require an exact, unique match of old_string.

ui_elements: No UI. Model-facing strings: "(lines <first>-<last> of <n>)\n" prefix; "(the file has <n> lines; start_line <first> is past the end)"; "\n…(truncated, <n> chars total; read the rest with start_line and line_count)"; list entries "…(truncated)" and "(empty)"; directories suffixed "/"
feature_notes: resolveURL: trims; empty -> "A file path is required."; "/" or "~" prefixes are absolute (tilde expanded), otherwise appended to the standardized root; path must equal root or start with root + "/" else "That path is outside the project. Stay inside <workingDirectory>.". Used by search_text too (per comment).

displayPath (lines 33-38): trimmed empty -> workingDirectory; `trimmed.hasPrefix(workingDirectory)` is a raw string prefix with no separator boundary, then ToolTitles.relativePath (ProviderSession.swift line 194-197) strips `root + "/"` only when present, else returns the path unchanged. So "/proj2/x" under "/proj" passes the prefix test but comes back unchanged, and displayPath(workingDirectory) returns workingDirectory itself; any other input returns the trimmed input.

readFile: resolveURL, then `FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath:)` (true for directories too, so a directory path gets whatever FileHandle(forReadingFrom:) or read(upToCount:) throws, not a Droppy message); missing -> "No such file: <display>."; reads in chunks of min(65_536, readLimit + 1 - count) until more than 1,000,000 bytes; over limit -> "That file is too large to read (<byteCount> bytes)." using seekToEnd; decode UTF-8 then ISO Latin-1 (`String(data: data, encoding: .utf8) ?? String(data: data, encoding: .isoLatin1)`), else "That file is not readable as text.".

readFile with startLine or lineCount: `text.split(separator: "
", omittingEmptySubsequences: false)` on a Swift String splits by Character, and "
" is one Character that is not equal to "
", so a CRLF file is not split (it is one "line": "(lines 1-1 of 1)" plus the whole file). Parity decision for the port: a JS split('
') would split CRLF files. first = max(1, startLine ?? 1); first > count -> "(the file has <n> lines; start_line <first> is past the end)"; count = max(1, lineCount ?? 200); returns "(lines first-last of total)
" plus the slice joined with "
".

readFile without range: returns text unchanged when `text.utf8.count <= 60_000` (UTF-8 bytes); otherwise characterCount = `text.count` (Swift grapheme clusters, not UTF-16 units) and if > 60,000 returns `String(text.prefix(60_000))` (first 60,000 grapheme clusters) plus "\n…(truncated, <characterCount> chars total; read the rest with start_line and line_count)". A JS .length/.slice port would cut and count differently.
writeFile: inside the Mutations actor; "Could not encode that content." if UTF-8 encoding fails; cancellation checked between each step.

editFile (lines 92-120), inside the Mutations actor: the empty-old check ("old_string must not be empty. Read the file first, then edit an exact block.") runs BEFORE resolveURL, so an empty old_string with an outside path gets the empty-old error. Reads with `String(contentsOf: url, encoding: .utf8)` and has no existence check: a missing or non-UTF-8 file throws Foundation's error, not a Droppy string, and Latin-1 files readFile accepts cannot be edited. Counts non-overlapping matches with `current.range(of: old, options: [], range: remaining)` on NSString: no .literalSearch, so canonically equivalent composed/decomposed sequences match (precomposed "é" matches "e" + combining accent) and ranges are UTF-16; a JS indexOf port is stricter. 0 -> "That exact text was not found in <display>. Read the file and copy it exactly."; >1 -> "That text appears <n> times in <display>. Include more context so it matches once."; replaces the single match and writes UTF-8 atomically.

listFiles: base = working directory when `path.trimmed.isEmpty`, else resolveURL(path); non-directory -> "No such directory: <displayPath(path.isEmpty ? workingDirectory : path)>." (untrimmed check here, though displayPath trims, so the text is the same). Recursive: FileManager enumerator with [.skipsHiddenFiles, .skipsPackageDescendants], in enumerator order (NOT sorted); any entry whose lastPathComponent is in skippedDirectories is skipped (skipDescendants) even when it is a FILE named e.g. build, dist or target; directories are not listed; entries are ToolTitles.relativePath(url.path, to: workingDirectory), i.e. relative to the project root, not to base. Non-recursive: contentsOfDirectory sorted with Swift String < (case-sensitive); drops names in skippedDirectories (files too) and names starting with ".DS_Store"; each entry is relativePath(full, to: workingDirectory) + "/" for directories, so listing "src" yields "src/a.swift", not bare names; other hidden files are kept. Both: `if results.count >= 300 { results.append("…(truncated)"); break }` fires on the 300th entry even if nothing follows, so exactly 300 entries return 301 lines with the marker. Empty -> "(empty)".
